I've been working this land for thirty years. I know what it needs and what I can handle. My husband and one of my kids do some work in town now, so I can't take on too much labor-heavy work myself. Cotton is hard — lots of hand-picking, pest management. I'll keep a small plot of it, maybe 2 mu, because it brings extra cash when prices are decent. But most of my land, 5 mu, stays in the wheat-maize rotation. That's what I know best and the market is steady for grain.

For wheat this winter, I'll use the improved variety I've been buying from the county seed station for the past several years — not hybrid, but reliable. I'll do three irrigations: once before winter sets in, once at jointing, once at heading. No point overdoing water, it costs electricity to pump. I apply fertilizer in two splits — basal at planting, topdress at jointing. Around 14 kg nitrogen per mu. I'll rotary till after maize harvest to break up the stubble.

For summer maize after wheat, I'll go with hybrid seed — the yield difference is real and the seed isn't that expensive. I'll direct seed after wheat harvest without full tillage, just to save time since there's only a short window. Two irrigations should be enough if summer rains cooperate. Eighteen kilos of nitrogen, side-dressed.

For cotton, I'll plant in April on the 2 mu I've set aside. It needs more attention — four irrigations, more sprays for bollworm and aphid. But I manage it myself slowly over the season. I'll rotary till that plot in spring.
